doc.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997

title: Mixed bands and visiting stars in Buffalo
summary: Players of both races worked together, major bands came through, and Chippewa Street is reviving.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: But when you got called for a particular kind of gig at that time, was it a mixture of players?

Oh yeah, oh sure. It was very healthy at the time in Buffalo. We all thought of course things aren’t happening, but back in those days they really were happening. It was like Miles and all of these bands, Dizzy, they were all coming to Buffalo. There was a venue for them there.

Oh yeah. There was a lot of places that really had top-notch, world-class musicians you know. And it was healthier in town. There was a lot of local things happening you know, and much healthier than it is now, although it’s picking up again in Buffalo. On the same street we mentioned, Chippewa, it’s like a rejuvenation. All the college people have discovered that area, and they’re all coming in and digging the music and hanging out and whatever they do you know. But it’s just coming back. In fact Don and I are playing there Friday night at this club right on Chippewa. And it’ll be mobbed. Of course they love Don in Buffalo. Me? I don’t know.
